answers.name: Hydrogen
answers.fact: About three-quarters of the normal matter in the universe.

answers.name: Helium
answers.fact: Spotted in the Sun's light before anyone found it on Earth.

answers.name: Carbon
answers.fact: Diamonds and pencil 'lead' are both pure carbon.

answers.name: Nitrogen
answers.fact: Makes up about 78% of the air.

answers.name: Oxygen
answers.fact: The most abundant element in Earth's crust.

answers.name: Sodium
answers.fact: Reacts violently with water, yet it's half of table salt.

answers.name: Iron
answers.fact: Earth's core is mostly iron.

answers.name: Copper
answers.fact: The Statue of Liberty's green skin is weathered copper.

answers.name: Silver
answers.fact: The best electrical conductor of any element.

answers.name: Gold
answers.fact: All the gold ever mined would fit in a cube about 22 metres across.

answers.name: Krypton
answers.fact: Real, despite Superman. The name is Greek for 'hidden'.

answers.name: Tungsten
answers.fact: The highest melting point of any metal: about 3,422 °C.

answers.name: Bismuth
answers.fact: Grows rainbow staircase crystals, and it's in Pepto-Bismol.

answers.name: Lithium
answers.fact: Light enough to float on oil.

answers.name: Boron
answers.fact: Gives borosilicate glass its resistance to heat.

answers.name: Fluorine
answers.fact: The most reactive element of all.

answers.name: Neon
answers.fact: Glows red-orange. Other 'neon' colours are usually other gases.

answers.name: Magnesium
answers.fact: Burns with a blinding white light, once used for camera flashes.

answers.name: Aluminium
answers.fact: Once pricier than gold. The Washington Monument is capped with it.

answers.name: Silicon
answers.fact: Silicon Valley is named after it.

answers.name: Phosphorus
answers.fact: Discovered in 1669 by an alchemist boiling down urine.

answers.name: Sulfur
answers.fact: Pure sulfur barely smells. The rotten-egg stink comes from its compounds.

answers.name: Chlorine
answers.fact: Used as a chemical weapon in World War I.

answers.name: Argon
answers.fact: About 1% of every breath you take.

answers.name: Potassium
answers.fact: Bananas are famous for it, but a potato has more.

answers.name: Calcium
answers.fact: The most abundant metal in your body.

answers.name: Titanium
answers.fact: As strong as some steels at roughly half the weight.

answers.name: Chromium
answers.fact: Makes rubies red and emeralds green.

answers.name: Manganese
answers.fact: Lies around the deep-sea floor in lumpy nodules.

answers.name: Cobalt
answers.fact: Named after the kobold, a troublesome goblin of German mines.

answers.name: Nickel
answers.fact: German miners called its ore 'Kupfernickel', or copper demon.

answers.name: Zinc
answers.fact: Galvanised steel is coated in zinc to stop rust.

answers.name: Arsenic
answers.fact: A favourite poison of Victorian murder plots.

answers.name: Tin
answers.fact: Bend a tin bar and it crackles: the 'tin cry'.

answers.name: Iodine
answers.fact: Added to table salt to prevent goitre.

answers.name: Xenon
answers.fact: Fuels the ion engines on some spacecraft.

answers.name: Barium
answers.fact: Patients drink a barium 'milkshake' so their gut shows up on X-rays.

answers.name: Platinum
answers.fact: Spanish conquistadors dismissed it as 'platina', little silver.

answers.name: Mercury
answers.fact: The only metal that's liquid at room temperature.

answers.name: Lead
answers.fact: Its Latin name, plumbum, gave us the word 'plumbing'.

answers.name: Polonium
answers.fact: Discovered by Marie Curie and named after her homeland, Poland.

answers.name: Radon
answers.fact: A radioactive gas that can build up in basements.

answers.name: Radium
answers.fact: Painted on glowing watch dials, poisoning the 'Radium Girls' who did the work.

answers.name: Uranium
answers.fact: Named after the planet Uranus.

answers.name: Plutonium
answers.fact: Named after Pluto, completing the set.

answers.name: Einsteinium
answers.fact: First found in the debris of the first hydrogen bomb test.

answers.name: Beryllium
answers.fact: Coats the mirrors of the James Webb Space Telescope.

answers.name: Scandium
answers.fact: Mendeleev predicted it before it was found.

answers.name: Vanadium
answers.fact: Named after Vanadís, another name for the Norse goddess Freyja.

answers.name: Gallium
answers.fact: Melts in your hand, at about 30 °C.

answers.name: Germanium
answers.fact: Named after Germany by the chemist who found it.

answers.name: Selenium
answers.fact: Named after Selene, the Greek goddess of the Moon.

answers.name: Bromine
answers.fact: One of only two elements that are liquid at room temperature.

answers.name: Rubidium
answers.fact: Named for the deep red lines in its spectrum.

answers.name: Strontium
answers.fact: Gives fireworks their red.

answers.name: Yttrium
answers.fact: Used in the red glow of old colour TV screens.

answers.name: Zirconium
answers.fact: Cubic zirconia, the diamond lookalike, is made from it.

answers.name: Niobium
answers.fact: Named after Niobe, daughter of Tantalus. It's always found with tantalum.

answers.name: Molybdenum
answers.fact: From the Greek for lead, which it was once mistaken for.

answers.name: Technetium
answers.fact: The first element made artificially, and the lightest with no stable form.

answers.name: Ruthenium
answers.fact: Named after Ruthenia, an old Latin name for Russia.

answers.name: Rhodium
answers.fact: Often the priciest precious metal, thanks to catalytic converters.

answers.name: Palladium
answers.fact: Named after the asteroid Pallas.

answers.name: Cadmium
answers.fact: Gives artists' paints their brightest yellows and reds.

answers.name: Indium
answers.fact: Makes touchscreens work, as indium tin oxide.

answers.name: Antimony
answers.fact: Ancient Egyptians used it in kohl eyeliner.

answers.name: Tellurium
answers.fact: Named after Tellus, the Latin word for Earth.

answers.name: Caesium
answers.fact: Atomic clocks use it to define the second.

answers.name: Lanthanum
answers.fact: Found in camera lenses and hybrid car batteries.

answers.name: Cerium
answers.fact: Lighter flints are mostly a cerium-based alloy.

answers.name: Praseodymium
answers.fact: Greek for 'green twin'.

answers.name: Neodymium
answers.fact: Makes the strongest permanent magnets there are.

answers.name: Promethium
answers.fact: Named after Prometheus. Almost none exists naturally on Earth.

answers.name: Samarium
answers.fact: Indirectly named after a person: a Russian mining official, via the mineral samarskite.

answers.name: Europium
answers.fact: Helps euro banknotes glow under UV as an anti-forgery check.

answers.name: Gadolinium
answers.fact: Injected as a contrast agent for MRI scans.

answers.name: Terbium
answers.fact: Named after the Swedish village of Ytterby, and used in green phosphors.

answers.name: Dysprosium
answers.fact: From the Greek for 'hard to get at'.

answers.name: Holmium
answers.fact: Named after Holmia, the Latin name for Stockholm.

answers.name: Erbium
answers.fact: Boosts the signal in long-distance fibre-optic cables.

answers.name: Lutetium
answers.fact: Named after Lutetia, the Latin name for Paris.

answers.name: Hafnium
answers.fact: Named after Hafnia, the Latin name for Copenhagen.

answers.name: Tantalum
answers.fact: Named after Tantalus, and found in the capacitors of nearly every phone.

answers.name: Rhenium
answers.fact: The last stable element to be discovered, in 1925.

answers.name: Osmium
answers.fact: The densest naturally occurring element.

answers.name: Iridium
answers.fact: A worldwide layer of it marks the asteroid strike that ended the dinosaurs.

answers.name: Thallium
answers.fact: Once used in rat poison, and nicknamed 'the poisoner's poison'.

answers.name: Astatine
answers.fact: So rare there's under a gram in Earth's whole crust at any moment.

answers.name: Francium
answers.fact: The last element discovered in nature, in 1939.

answers.name: Actinium
answers.fact: Glows pale blue in the dark.

answers.name: Thorium
answers.fact: Named after Thor.

answers.name: Neptunium
answers.fact: Named after Neptune, the next planet out from Uranus.

answers.name: Americium
answers.fact: Sits inside most household smoke detectors.

answers.name: Curium
answers.fact: Named after Marie and Pierre Curie.

answers.name: Berkelium
answers.fact: Named after Berkeley, California.

answers.name: Californium
answers.fact: Used as a neutron source to start up nuclear reactors.

answers.name: Fermium
answers.fact: Also found in that H-bomb debris, and named after Enrico Fermi.

answers.name: Mendelevium
answers.fact: Named after Dmitri Mendeleev, father of the periodic table.

answers.name: Nobelium
answers.fact: Named after Alfred Nobel.

answers.name: Lawrencium
answers.fact: Named after Ernest Lawrence, inventor of the cyclotron.

answers.name: Rutherfordium
answers.fact: Named after New Zealand-born physicist Ernest Rutherford.

answers.name: Dubnium
answers.fact: Named after Dubna, a Russian town built around nuclear research.

answers.name: Seaborgium
answers.fact: Named after Glenn Seaborg while he was still alive.

answers.name: Bohrium
answers.fact: Named after Danish physicist Niels Bohr.

answers.name: Darmstadtium
answers.fact: Named after the German city of Darmstadt.

answers.name: Copernicium
answers.fact: Named after the astronomer Nicolaus Copernicus.

answers.name: Nihonium
answers.fact: The first element discovered in Asia, named after Japan, 'Nihon'.

answers.name: Flerovium
answers.fact: Named after Soviet physicist Georgy Flyorov.

answers.name: Moscovium
answers.fact: Named after the Moscow region.

answers.name: Livermorium
answers.fact: Named after the Lawrence Livermore lab in California.

answers.name: Oganesson
answers.fact: The heaviest known element, named after physicist Yuri Oganessian in his lifetime.

answers.name: Thulium
answers.fact: Named after Thule, a mythical land in the far north.

answers.name: Protactinium
answers.fact: One of the rarest and priciest naturally occurring elements.

answers.name: Hassium
answers.fact: Named after the German state of Hesse.

answers.name: Meitnerium
answers.fact: Named after Lise Meitner, who helped discover nuclear fission.

answers.name: Roentgenium
answers.fact: Named after Wilhelm Röntgen, discoverer of X-rays.

answers.name: Tennessine
answers.fact: Named after the US state of Tennessee.

answers.name: Ytterbium
answers.fact: One of four elements named after the same tiny Swedish village, Ytterby.
